source_review.notes: Checked current official NASA Logical Decomposition, System Design, functional/timing/state routing, Stakeholder Expectations, Technical Requirements and Interface Management guidance; active NASA-HDBK-1009A; final OMG SysML 2.0; current NASA Software Engineering Handbook Version D requirements-analysis guidance; and final NIST IR 8539 (2025). All ten final URLs returned HTTP 200. Claims are bounded to complementary behavior views, action/flow/state/interaction semantics, transition-model analysis, model checking and configured empirical validation.

evidence: Reviewed the labeled transition-system tuple, execution trace, satisfaction relation, enabled-transition set, determinism/completeness cardinality, partial ordering and generic latency composition.
Confirmed state, initial state, events, inputs/outputs, transitions, guards/effects, invariants and time remain distinct.
Confirmed system-property conclusions are explicitly bounded by abstraction, environment, fairness, modeled state and tool semantics.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation supports structured analysis without claiming that one formalism captures every human, physical, environmental or adversarial phenomenon.

evidence: Executed behavior-transition-integrity-check and reproduced five states and eight transitions.
Recomputed eight unique state-event pairs, five reachable states from OFF, zero unreachable states, zero duplicate-pair guard proxies and zero nonterminal dead ends when SAFE is declared terminal.
Confirmed SAFE is reachable through startup timeout, RUNNING major fault and DEGRADED escalation paths.
Recomputed eight nonempty requirement traces and behavior_model_structurally_consistent exact output.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The transition table has no explicit guards, timing, outputs, invariants, concurrency, sensor model or physics; its counts cannot establish real safe behavior.

evidence: Confirmed transition enablement depends jointly on source state, event and guard valuation rather than event labels alone.
Confirmed determinism permits at most one enabled transition while completeness may require exactly one only for every admissible modeled condition.
Confirmed absence of a precedence relation permits concurrency but does not establish independence because resources and data can still constrain order.
Confirmed end-to-end latency is intentionally represented by an unspecified composition over durations, queues, scheduling, network, humans and uncertainty rather than naïve summation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Intentional nondeterminism remains allowed when resolution semantics and universal property obligations are explicit.

evidence: Challenged happy-path-only scenarios, incomplete actions, hidden item/resource flows, sequence-diagram exhaustiveness, mode/state/lifecycle conflation and absent initialization/termination.
Reviewed guard gaps/overlap, simultaneous events, event priority, unhandled events, nondeterminism, unreachable states, deadlock, livelock, impossible joins and unsafe recovery.
Reviewed concurrency, races, shared resources, priority inversion, queues, retry storms, idempotency, cancellation, backpressure, clock domains, drift, jitter and diagram-position timing assumptions.
Reviewed human authority/workload/handoff, degraded/manual/emergency modes, missed/false detection, common cause, late safe-state entry, adversarial behavior and physical-model discrepancy.
Reviewed model-checking abstraction/fairness/state reduction, finite simulation coverage, generated implementation, variants/refinement and operational divergence.
Reviewed all ten examples and five answers for semantic scope, off-nominal paths, bounded analysis, evidence correspondence and change propagation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Consequential behavior still needs applicable stakeholder, domain, software, hardware, operations, human-factors, safety, security, privacy, timing, reliability, interface, V&V and technical-authority review.

evidence: Traced purpose, boundary, configuration, actors/environment and abstraction from scenario framing through formal and empirical evidence.
Confirmed scenario, activity, interaction, state/mode, timing and algorithm views remain complementary with explicit semantic roles.
Confirmed actions, transitions, concurrency, time, resources, humans and off-nominal behavior retain required inputs/effects/conditions and ownership.
Confirmed requirements/properties, model structure, simulation, model checking, tests and operational observations remain separate evidence layers.
Confirmed refinement, variants, baselines, toolchain, generated artifacts, change impact and contradictory field evidence stay governed.
invariant_checking.notes: A structurally consistent behavior model can still be operationally incomplete or unsafe; the chapter repeats that distinction at every evidence transition.

proof_review.notes: The chapter describes formal property verification but presents no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed reachable, deterministic, complete, safe, live, deadlock-free, verified, validated, exhaustive, representative, equivalent and conforming language for scope and assumptions.
artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-053/report.json records exact execution evidence for one declared transition table and graph checks only.
The chapter requires configured prototypes/tests/logs/telemetry, aligned clocks/state mappings, uncertainties and coverage for real-behavior claims.
A model-checked property is always phrased as a property of a formalized model under declared abstraction and environment, not proof of deployed security or safety.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external review is claimed, and the checker cannot evaluate timing, guards, concurrency, hydraulics, sensor coverage, human behavior or safe-state adequacy.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked behavior, behavior model, scenario/use case, activity/flow, interaction/sequence, state, mode, event, guard, transition, concurrency, timing, nondeterminism, deadlock, livelock, safety/liveness and model checking. The chapter consistently treats the views as complementary and separates formal-model truth from real-system validity.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked scenario grounding, action/flow semantics, interactions, states/modes, transitions, nondeterminism, concurrency, timing, resources/data, humans, fault behavior, properties, structural checks, simulation, formal verification, validation, traceability, refinement and generation/change. Cases cover clinical exceptions, guard overlap, deadlock, retry storms, modes, physical timing, handoff, access policy, variants and telemetry oscillation.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from operational questions through semantic views, off-nominal assurance, analysis/evidence and lifecycle integration. Ten examples and five complete solutions require learners to design a rail-door behavior set, repair an unsafe state machine, analyze payment concurrency, bound formal security evidence and diagnose an operator-overloading recovery loop.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, systems-modeling, formal-methods, software, hardware, operations, human-factors, safety, security, privacy, reliability, timing, interface, verification, validation, or technical-authority review is claimed.
